av_event.what: While Kerry talks about her children, Charlotte's smile fades. She looks down and away to the left of the camera for about three seconds, then looks back up with her smile back in place.

text:
B: Hi! Hello, can you hear me okay? Sorry, I wasn't sure if it had started.
A: Yeah, hi, I can hear you fine. I wasn't sure either, to be fair.
B: Oh good. I'm Charlotte, I'm in Woking, so Surrey. Erm, is it just three minutes, is that right?
A: Yeah, I think so. I'm Kerry, I'm in Stowmarket, in Suffolk.
B: Oh lovely. I don't think I've ever been to Suffolk, sorry, that's terrible. So what do you do, are you working at the moment?
A: Erm, yeah, I do admin for a plumbing and heating firm. Part-time, just mornings mostly. Answering the phone, booking in boiler services, that sort of thing.
B: Oh, the phones. I bet you get some cross people this time of year.
A: Oh, all the time. Someone's boiler's gone and they've got kids in the house, and you sort of just have to stay calm, you know, and tell them we'll get someone out. Most of them are alright once you've talked to them.
B: That's so true. I'm in operations, so I look after nine dental practices across Surrey and Hampshire, and honestly half my job is complaints. Patients, staff, suppliers, everyone. Do you know what I mean? You end up being the person everyone rings.
A: Nine, gosh. That's a lot.
B: It is, it's a lot of driving. The A3 this morning was an absolute nightmare. But I like it, I sort of like being busy. Sorry, I'm rambling. Did you do the puzzle bit at the start?
A: Yeah, I didn't get very far with it, to be honest. I sort of gave up on the last one.
B: Oh, thank God, me too. I was sat there going, is this testing something, am I failing?
A: Same. I thought it was just me.
B: No, definitely not. Erm, so is that your cat in the background? I saw it in your photo, the ginger one.
A: Yeah, that's Biscuit. He's just asleep on the settee as usual. He brought a mouse in again yesterday, so he's in my bad books.
B: No way, our dog's called Biscuit! He's a cockapoo.
A: Oh, that's funny. Great minds.
B: Honestly. He chewed a cushion this week, so they're both in trouble. Do you have kids? Sorry, I saw the book bag.
A: Yeah, two. Ellie's twelve, she's in Year 8, and Josh is nine. Ellie's on at us for a phone with TikTok at the minute, we keep arguing about it. Every night. Darren says no, I sort of say maybe, so she just comes to me, you know.
B: That sounds like such a tricky one. I think I'd be the maybe parent as well, to be honest.
A: Yeah, it's the guilt, isn't it. Everyone else in her class has got it, apparently.
B: Apparently! That's what they all say. Erm, do you work from home at all, or is it all in the office?
A: No, it's in the office, on the industrial estate. It's only ten minutes. My mum helps with pick-ups so it works out.
B: That's lovely, having your mum close. I'm on the phone to mine most days. Tom teases me about it.
A: Is Tom your husband?
B: Yes, sorry, yeah. He's a quantity surveyor. He cycles to work, which I hate. I'm convinced he's going to get knocked off.
A: Oh, I'd worry too. Darren's an electrician so he's in the van all day. He got stuck on the A14 last week for about two hours.
B: Two hours! See, I'd be texting him constantly. Is this the sort of thing we're meant to talk about, do you think?
A: I think so, I think it's just chatting. Yeah, so...
B: Okay, good. I always feel like I'm doing it wrong. What are you watching at the moment, anything good?
A: Erm, Married at First Sight mostly. And Love Island when it's on. Darren hates it.
